nodes.label: The Collector's Table (Creative North Star)
nodes.rationale: StudyQuest is a collection, not a dashboard; the interface refuses both the gamified card-grid cliche and the monochrome product-tool clone by making colour a claim about earned mastery rather than decoration.

nodes.label: Rarity Is Mastery (semantic colour scale)
nodes.rationale: A hue on the surface is always a claim about what a student has earned; this is what makes the palette semantic rather than merely pretty, and is derived by a single function rather than assigned by hand.

nodes.label: setRarity(cardCount, dueCount)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately conservative: a set with no due cards stays common because a bare zero cannot distinguish 'mastered' from 'never opened', and rarity must not make a claim the data does not support.

nodes.label: The Frame-Carries-Rarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Rarity is printed into the cut edge and inset keyline, never a coloured stripe/rail/bar, because a coloured side stripe above 1px is the single most recognisable tell of a generated interface; on a real trading card the frame itself is the rarity.

nodes.label: The Amber Rule
nodes.rationale: Amber means Study Coins and legendary mastery only; a streak, score, card count or timer never takes gold, keeping the currency colour meaningful.

nodes.label: The Ink Variant Rule
nodes.rationale: Plain coral measures 3.01:1 on the table and fails AA for anything but large text, so any rarity hue used as text must switch to its -ink variant.

nodes.label: The Two-Value Ground Rule
nodes.rationale: Only table and stock exist as grounds, both warm (R>G>B) in both themes, because a neutral grey anywhere turns the product back into a form.

nodes.label: The Hue-Is-Never-The-Only-Signal Rule
nodes.rationale: No state is announced by colour alone, because the audience includes younger teenagers and phone-first readers, so every colour-coded state carries a second cue (underline, label, hatch, words).

nodes.label: The Struck-and-Read Rule
nodes.rationale: Archivo carries anything struck (headings, titles, numbers) and Schibsted Grotesk carries anything read, keeping typographic roles unambiguous.

nodes.label: The Measurement Rule
nodes.rationale: Any coin, timer, score or count takes tabular lining numerals (.num) so a ticking value never nudges layout.

nodes.label: The Pip-and-Total Rule
nodes.rationale: Large numerals are reserved for the four StatStrip totals; everything else is a struck pip, because seven label-plus-big-number cells stacked together is the hero-metric scaffold the product refuses.

nodes.label: The No-Kicker Rule
nodes.rationale: No small-caps/uppercase kicker sits above a heading; a heading must carry its own weight.

nodes.label: The Next-Action-First Rule
nodes.rationale: The first viewport puts the decision of what to study now before any summary, total or history.

nodes.label: The Earned-Stock Rule
nodes.rationale: Card stock represents real, studied material; an unbuilt feature (the Arena) gets no frame at all, because giving it card stock would be a quiet door claiming to be furniture.

nodes.label: The Earned-Foil Rule
nodes.rationale: Foil is the system's one material effect and appears only at legendary rank; adding it elsewhere spends the only currency the visual system has.

nodes.label: The Real-Offset Rule
nodes.rationale: Every shadow has a real vertical offset and warm tint; zero-offset halos or coloured glows read as a screenshot pasted onto the table.

nodes.label: The One Primary Rule
nodes.rationale: Only one primary (brushed-sheen) button may be in view, so the main action stays unmistakable without being the loudest object on screen.

nodes.label: The Icon Weight Rule
nodes.rationale: Bold icons for actions/navigation, fill icons for things owned/earned, because solid glyphs read as objects and outlined glyphs read as actions in a collection-based product.

nodes.label: The Rarity Frame (signature component)
nodes.rationale: The one irreducible component: a card whose cut edge and inset keyline carry the rarity its content earned, with foil at the top step, letting a library read as a collection at a glance.

nodes.label: accentFor() (deprecated hash-to-hue helper)
nodes.rationale: A vestige of the previous (Ink & Gold) system that assigns decorative per-item colour by hashing a string; directly contradicts the Rarity Rule and must not be wired to anything.
